```plato

//==
// # Polar and figure curves in 2D
//
// The named plane curves whose natural description is a radius as a function of
// angle — roses, cardioids, limacons, lemniscates, and the classical trisecting
// and conchoidal cubics — together with the two figure curves (Lissajous,
// butterfly) that are drawn the same way. Most are `IPolarCurve2D`, so a single
// RadiusAt body is their whole implementation; those live in
// `curves-shapes.library.plato`. Every type is in canonical position about
// the origin and is placed elsewhere with a transform.

//==
// # Polar and figure curves

// The rose r = Radius * cos(PetalFrequency * theta). A whole odd frequency k
// yields k petals; a whole even k yields 2k petals; fractional frequencies
// close only over multiple turns
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rose_(mathematics)).
type RoseCurve2D
    implements IPolarCurve2D
{
    Radius: Number;
    PetalFrequency: Number;
}
```
